Address a code review of PR #527 (change 325, branch `fix/degraded-results-are-not-kept`, head bd16ed31, trail 469) in the caliper repo. In your worktree: `git fetch origin`, `git switch -c fix-527e origin/fix/degraded-results-are-not-kept`; push with `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/fix/degraded-results-are-not-kept` (normal fast-forward; NEVER force). You OWN crates/core/src/dependency_types.rs and crates/core/src/dependency_types/** (incl. ledger.rs), crates/core/src/pipeline/revision/lazy.rs, crates/core/src/pipeline/semantic_hook.rs, crates/core/src/types/semantic/** and the fallback sites in crates/semantic/src/lib.rs (~790-840) only; touch nothing else (#523 edits extractor/**). Read first: /Users/gabe/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-caliper/memory/worker-contract.md, perf-priority-wall-then-memory.md, evidence-types-direction.md and diagnose-after-three-findings.md, AGENTS.md (non-negotiable 6), CONTRIBUTING.md, `gh pr view 527`, /tmp/claude-501/pr-degraded.md (rounds 1-4: one `ReadLedger` per layer; `Settled::Degraded` re-ask with 30 s `DEGRADED_RETRY` backoff). Rules: signed commits with trailer `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED`; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` first; one cargo process at a time; scratch under /tmp/claude-501/ (build your own gate fixture: `node scripts/gate_fixtures.mjs /tmp/claude-501/fix527e/gate-large`); update the PR body FILE /tmp/claude-501/pr-degraded.md in place ('Round 5'); keep/extend the changeset; I publish the body and resolve findings. Final message max 170 words: head SHA, per item CONFIRMED (failing test)/refuted/dismissed, blockers. Cap 120 tool calls; never ask questions. Every fix keeps the ledger model (one source of truth) and must not cause new classes of finding: grep the sibling sites and add parity tests.

THE REVIEW (verify each with a failing test on bd16ed31 first):
(1) PERF, wall time matters most: while any walk stays unread, a component is never memoized, `grow` runs on every request and `inherit_memos` discards EVERY memo in the session (lazy.rs ~1306: `any_unread()`): one permanently unreadable `.d.ts` (EACCES) makes every request cost two resolutions plus a layer extension, grows the layer chain toward MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH and regresses first-answer latency for the whole session, including components that never touch the bad file. Fix: (a) `inherit_memos` drops only memos of components whose transitive demands include a Failed ledger entry (the ledger already marks walk nodes), keeping all others; (b) a persistently failing path is retried on a backoff (mirror the checker side's `DEGRADED_RETRY`, injectable clock/counter, never wall time in tests) or until the file's mtime/size changes or an edit event arrives, so repeated requests for a component behind a failed read do not redo `grow` each time. Tests: exact counts of `grow`/resolutions across N requests with one permanently unreadable file (unrelated components: zero extra work and memos kept; affected component: at most one retry within the backoff; after the file is readable and the backoff passes or an edit arrives: the full answer equals cold). Report the request cost before/after. (2) An outcome with no entry for the component (a run past the heap budget, or a skipped target) is still kept as `Settled::Answered(Answered{component: None..})` and cached; a heap-budget run (Warning diagnostic, no component or fallback) then sticks until a file changes even after memory pressure is gone. Round 2 made `unavailable` an explicit marker so a real empty answer is not mistaken for an outage; the question now is what a BUDGET-EXCEEDED or SKIPPED run is. Inspect how the semantic crate reports over-budget and skipped targets (diagnostic codes/severities in crates/semantic): if the run is a budget or resource failure (not a verdict about this component), mark it transient with the same explicit-marker approach (set where the budget decision is made, never inferred from absence) so it is not cached or stored and is retried on the backoff; a target the pass legitimately skips (not part of the program, not a component) stays a kept answer. Test both with exact assertions; if the codes make the distinction impossible, say exactly why in the PR body. (3) A rejected `module_exports` (lib.rs ~815) is marked transient but keeps the reason 'not part of the checker's program' and drops the rejection message: every other Rejected site says `the checker rejected a request: {message}`; carry the message and do not state a verdict. Test the exact diagnostic text. (4) The cold-load index is written only when no read failed (`!loader.ledger.any_failed()`, dependency_types.rs ~1384), so one persistently unreadable file disables index learning for every later cold load (a cost the fewer-fs-calls work removed): persist the entries whose walks are COMPLETE (not marked in the ledger) and skip only the incomplete ones. Test: a package with one unreadable file and several complete walks: the index contains exactly the complete walks, a second cold run uses them (assert the fs-call/probe count drops) and equals the cold answer. (5) Add the missing test the mutation run found: within ONE load, a failed read of F followed by a successful read of F through another path keeps F Failed (the answers derived from the failed read are incomplete): assert it, and in the PR body state this is deliberate (the cost is one skipped index entry and a warning until the next load re-reads it). DISMISS with a one-line reason each in the PR body (no code change): (6) the removed once-per-session warning: each degraded answer carries the warning tagged `affects=[that component]`, so the N warnings are N true statements, one per degraded component, and the output dedups identical ones; (7) the findings about code on main or other open PRs, listed so they are tracked, not dropped: `reroot` not releasing snapshots when it fails part-way (#515), `BatchAnswers` slot memory (#513), `member_name` applied only to object fields (#519), the flights walk-0 default (#513/#526): say they are not in this PR's diff and are follow-ups. VERIFY: output byte-identical (JSON parsed, `stats` dropped) vs a build of origin/main on /Users/gabe/.cache/caliper/corpora/repos/{mantine/packages/@mantine/core/src,chakra-ui/packages/react/src} (healthy runs must not change; drop runs with a SEMANTIC_BACKEND entry of severity other than info, by code and severity); gates by exit code: `just lint doc-check machete typos`, `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast` (pty/watch tests need the sandbox off), `just test-checker-lane` (outside the sandbox, no CARGO_TARGET_DIR), `gate_harness determinism` and `memory --tsc built-in` on your own fixture; run tests/session_equals_cold.rs from `origin/test/session-equals-cold` against your tree without committing it. Mutation-prove each new rule.

</system-reminder>

content.content:
1	## What
2	
3	Two shared-state defects where a transient failure was stored as an answer. Both confirmed by tests that fail on `origin/main` (`f4a88f93`).
4	
5	**1. A checker outage was kept as the component's answer** (`crates/core/src/pipeline/semantic_hook.rs`; audit shared-state hit 1, semantic-wire hit 1).
6	
7	- Cause: `read_outcome` turned an outcome with no component and no fallback (`SemanticOutcome::unavailable`: timeout, crash, checker not running) into `Answered { component: None, diagnostics: [] }`, and `ask` inserted every `Answered` into `cache.answers`. The warning went to a once-per-session `warned` flag. Every later request until a source edit got structural props, no diagnostic, `awaits_checker` false.
8	- Fix: the notion is a type. `Settled` gains `Degraded(Vec<Diagnostic>)`; `read_outcome` returns it for an outcome that answers nothing. `ask` inserts only `Settled::Answered`. `refine` attaches a degraded request's diagnostics (each with `affects` = the component) to every answer it affects. The `warned` flag is gone. The next request asks the checker again.
9	- `awaits_checker` stays false on a degraded answer: a checker that stays down (`MAX_RESTARTS`, could not start) answers at once, so a host that re-asked on `awaits_checker` would loop. Not caching is what makes the next request ask again.
10	
11	**2. A failed dependency read was persisted as "not exported"** (`crates/core/src/dependency_types.rs`; audit shared-state hit 4).
12	
13	- Cause: `Loader::read` returned `None` on an I/O error, the `parsed` `OnceLock` stored `None`, `find_export_uncached` returned `None` without `cut`, the miss was cached, `learn`ed and written by `write_index` as `(module, name, None)`. Later runs trusted it while `package.json` was unchanged.
14	- Fix:
15	  - `read_text` returns `Err(Unreadable)` for a file that exists but cannot be read (still reports the Warning diagnostic once, as before). `parse_source` returns `Result<Option<_>, Unreadable>` and does not initialize the `parsed` cell on a failed read, so the next caller reads again.
16	  - `find_export_uncached` treats `Unreadable` as a cut (the cycle-cut mechanism): the miss is returned but neither kept, `learn`ed nor persisted.
17	  - The layer keeps only initialized `parsed` cells (`load`), so a session's next revision reads the file again instead of finding `None` in its parent.
18	  - `write_index` writes nothing when any dependency read failed in the run: an augmentation search's answer can hold the failure as an absence.
19	
20	Invariant: a failure to read or to ask is unknown, never absence; nothing derived from it enters a cache, a layer or the index.
21	
22	## Evidence
23	
24	Tests (each fails on `origin/main`, passes here):
25	
26	- `semantic_hook::a_request_the_checker_did_not_answer_is_asked_again_and_answered`: a fake provider returns `SemanticOutcome::unavailable(..)` for the first request, `finds_size` for the second. Request 2 carries `["label", "size"]`, equal (props and diagnostics) to a fresh session that never saw the outage. Base: `["label"]`.
27	- `semantic_hook::an_unavailable_checker_warns_on_every_answer_it_affects_and_never_fails_a_request` (replaces `..._warns_once_per_session_...`): Button, Card, Button again each carry one `SemanticBackend` Warning with `affects` = that key; 3 provider requests. Base: Card had none.
28	- `semantic_join::an_unavailable_checker_is_reported_to_the_story_that_joined_the_request_and_to_every_later_one` (was `..._reported_once_...`): warnings (1, 1). Base: (1, 0).
29	- `dependency_types::tests::an_export_in_a_file_that_could_not_be_read_is_found_on_the_next_run` (unix, `chmod 000` then restore): the unreadable run reports one Warning for the file; a session extension of that layer (demand from another directory) finds the export; the next cold run with the cache on finds it, equal to the oracle run with `use_cache: false`. Base: `(false, Some(NotExported))`.
30	- `dependency_types::augmentation_tests::a_file_an_augmentation_search_could_not_read_is_searched_again_on_the_next_run`: next run's `augmenters_of(reexp)` = `[inner/index.d.ts]`, equal to the cache-off oracle. Base: `[]`.
31	
32	Mutation proof (each guard removed, a test fails):
33	
34	- drop `*cut = true` on `Unreadable` -> `an_export_in_a_file_that_could_not_be_read_is_found_on_the_next_run` fails.
35	- drop the `write_index` gate -> `a_file_an_augmentation_search_could_not_read_is_searched_again_on_the_next_run` fails.
36	- keep uninitialized `parsed` cells in the layer as `None` -> `an_export_in_a_file_that_could_not_be_read_is_found_on_the_next_run` fails.
37	
38	Gates (exit codes):
39	
40	- `just lint doc-check machete typos`: exit 0.
41	- `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast` (sandbox off): exit 0, 1745 passed, 3 skipped.
42	- `just test-checker-lane` (no `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`): exit 0.
43	- `gate_harness determinism --tsc built-in` on `gate_fixtures.mjs` output in scratch: exit 0, 150 components, 9 variants (1/2/4 threads, reversed), all `equalsFirst`, 148 answered by the checker.
44	- `gate_harness memory --tsc built-in`: exit 0, 650 edits, 650 answered by the checker, 0 stale, `finalEqualsFresh`, peak RSS 361 MiB.
45	- Output vs a release build of `origin/main` (`extract --src <dir> --json --quiet --no-cache`, JSON parsed, `stats` dropped): identical on mantine `@mantine/core/src` (348 components) and chakra-ui `packages/react/src` (629 components). Neither run had a `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` diagnostic with severity other than info (checked by code and severity), so no run was dropped.
46	- Load during the gates: 1-minute average 19-69 on a shared machine; no timing was taken.
47	
48	Sweep, other places that keep an outcome or a read (not changed here, for the next fix to use the `Degraded`/`Unreadable` notion):
49	
50	- `crates/semantic/src/kept.rs:334` `save`: skips an outcome with diagnostics, so an `unavailable` one is not kept, but an outcome whose fallbacks came from `CallError::Rejected` (a tsrs panic, `STOPPED`, a decode error) has no diagnostics and is saved to the kept-answer file. Called from `lib.rs:216-229` (`resolve_cached`).
51	- `crates/semantic/src/lib.rs:838` turns `CallError::Rejected` (including `checker.rs:568` `STOPPED` and a caught panic) into a `SemanticFallback`. The hook caches a fallback as an answer, so a component asked while the checker panicked keeps that Info fallback until an edit. Fix belongs there (or in `on_demand.rs::answer` when `!backend.is_alive()` after the request): emit no fallback for a rejection caused by a stopped checker, so the outcome reads as degraded. Not done here: `lib.rs` is another worker's, and no test can inject a panicking built-in backend into `OnDemand` without a new seam.
52	- `dependency_types.rs` `Loader::demand` -> `unresolved_cause_in` (`self.parse(module)?`): an unreadable module yields `NotExported` in `unresolved`, which the layer keeps, and the demand is in `demands`, so a session does not re-run that exact demand until the layer is rebuilt. Not persisted (`unresolved` is never written).
53	- `dependency_types.rs` `augmentation_scan` (`self.read(file)?`) and `find_augmenting_files`: an unreadable file is skipped and the module's augmenter list without it is kept in `augmenters` for the run and its layer. No longer persisted (the `write_index` gate).
54	- `load_declaration`, `load_augmentations`, the React path of `demand`, and the `named`/`react_files` passes in `load` use `parse` and skip an unreadable file without caching anything derived from it.
55	
56	## Round 2
57	
58	Review of `b70e8f38`, fixed at the class level. Each item has a test that fails without the fix (mutation proof below).
59	
60	**1. A failed read is a type every consumer must handle** (`crates/core/src/dependency_types.rs`). CONFIRMED (session path), PARTLY REFUTED (index path).
61	
62	- `Unreadable` is now `ReadFailed`. `Loader::read`, `parse`, `parse_source`, `augmentation_scan`, `find_augmenting_files`, `augmenting_files`, `find_export(_in, _uncached)`, `unresolved_cause(_in)`, `load_declaration`, `load_augmentations`, `module_demand` and the new `follow` return `Result<_, ReadFailed>`; the `.ok().flatten()` wrappers are gone, so a new consumer cannot drop it silently.
63	- Every consumer and its decision:
64	  - `parse_source`: the per-file cell holds the read's result, the failure included, for this load only; `load` keeps only `Ok` cells in the layer, so the next load reads the file again.
65	  - `find_export_in` / `find_export_uncached` (export walk, `export *` included): `Err` propagates; nothing on the walk is inserted in `exports` or `learn`ed.
66	  - `unresolved_cause_in`: `Err` propagates; no `NotExported` enters `unresolved`.
67	  - `follow` (React path, export path, module path): `Err` puts the demand key in `failed`; `load` leaves `failed` keys out of the layer's `demands`, so `missing` returns them and a session's next load follows them again.
68	  - `load_declaration` (claim): `Err` before any claim, so nothing enters `claimed`, `declaring` or `react_files`; the demand that called it is `failed`.
69	  - `augmentation_scan` (entry, React-mentioning and re-export-only files): one `ScanCell` per file holds the scan, the failure included, for this load; never in the layer.
70	  - `find_augmenting_files` / `augmenting_files`: `Err` propagates; the list is not inserted in `augmenters` or `augmenter_crossed`, so neither the layer nor the index holds it.
71	  - `module_demand`: the `(scope, specifier)` cell now holds the parsed augmenting files or `ReadFailed`, so every demand of the scope, not only the first, is `failed` alike.
72	  - `load` (`files` and `react_files` passes): read the cells a successful claim initialized; `Ok(Some)` only.
73	  - `resolve` (`resolutions`): does not call `read`; oxc_resolver stats files, so a resolution is not derived from a failed read. Kept; the table test asserts every resolution equals the oracle's.
74	- `DependencyLayer::degraded` = a read failed in this load or a layer below; `write_index` runs only when `!degraded`. Refuted part of the finding: `write_index` already ran only for a cold load (`previous == None`), so a child load never wrote the index on its parent's behalf; the marker is carried anyway. No test fails when the gate is removed, since nothing derived from a failed read reaches the loader's maps any more; it is defence in depth.
75	- `scan`'s `parse_source(file, Some(source)).ok().flatten()` could not hide a failure (it passes the text, so it never reads); it is now `?` like the rest.
76	
77	**2. A degraded answer is held as a short-lived refusal** (`crates/core/src/pipeline/semantic_hook.rs`). CONFIRMED.
78	
79	- `AnswerCache::degraded`: `(key, stamp) -> (when, diagnostics)`, separate from `answers`. `find` returns `Found::Degraded` within `DEGRADED_RETRY` (30 s): the structural props plus the same diagnostics, without asking the checker. After it, or after `invalidate` (any source change, which clears it), the next request asks again; a recovered checker's answer is kept as usual.
80	- The clock is a `Clock` field (`Instant::now`), replaced in the unit test.
81	- `awaits_checker` stays false on a degraded answer: it means "ask again and you get the checker's props", which is false for 30 s; the Warning (`degradedBy` in the addon) tells the host the answer is degraded. A host that polled on `awaits_checker` would spin for the whole retry.
82	
83	**3. Unavailability is a mark, not an absence** (`crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs`). CONFIRMED.
84	
85	- `SemanticOutcome::unavailable: Option<Unavailable>`; `Unavailable(())` has a private field, so only `SemanticOutcome::unavailable(..)` can set it. `read_outcome` decides from it alone; an outcome with no entry for the key (a skipped target, a run past its heap budget) is `Settled::Answered` and kept.
86	
87	**4. One read per file per load** (`parse_source`, `augmentation_scan`). CONFIRMED.
88	
89	- The read happens inside the cell's `get_or_init`; callers that meet wait for the first and get its result, a failed read included. A file both parsed and scanned by callers that meet can still be read once by each reader kind (as on `origin/main`).
90	
91	**5. A transient fallback is never kept** (`crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs`, `crates/semantic/src/lib.rs`, `crates/semantic/src/kept.rs`). CONFIRMED.
92	
93	- `SemanticFallback::transient: bool`. `lib.rs` `rejected_fallback_of` sets it for `CallError::Rejected` in `answer_file`, at both sites: a component's request (~838) and `module_exports` (~796, which also merged a rejection into "not part of the checker's program").
94	- `SemanticOutcome::is_degraded()` = unavailable or any transient fallback. `to_bytes` refuses a degraded outcome (its marks are not stored), so `kept::save` writes nothing for it; that is the one owner. The hook reads a transient fallback for the asked key as `Settled::Degraded`.
95	
96	Tests (each fails with its guard removed):
97	
98	- `dependency_types::tests::a_file_that_could_not_be_read_is_read_again_by_the_next_load_on_every_path`: rows `ExportWalk`, `Claim` (index answered the export, warm run first), `EntryScan`, `ReExportScan`, `AugmentingScan`; `chmod 000`, cache on. Per row: the file is reported, the layer is `degraded`, its answers differ from the oracle's, and the session's next load (`missing` demands over the layer) and the next cold run equal the oracle (cache off): followed, files loaded, unresolved reasons, resolutions, `reexp`'s augmenters.
99	- `dependency_types::tests::readers_that_meet_read_a_file_once_and_share_its_result`: 8 threads, a 50 ms pause inside the read, `Parse` and `Scan`, readable and `chmod 000`: one read each time, 8 equal results.
100	- `pipeline::semantic_hook::tests::a_checker_that_answered_nothing_is_asked_again_only_after_the_retry_or_an_edit`: rows `Down`, `Rejected` (degraded) and `Verdict`, `Absent` (kept). 5 requests ask once; at retry - 1 ms not asked; at the retry asked (degraded) or not (kept); after `invalidate` asked; a recovered checker's props replace a degraded answer and are then kept.
101	- `kept::tests::a_transient_fallback_is_not_kept_and_a_verdict_is`.
102	- Changed: `semantic_hook` `an_unavailable_checker_warns_on_every_answer_it_affects_and_never_fails_a_request` (2 requests, not 3), `a_request_the_checker_did_not_answer_is_asked_again_and_answered` (the second request is refused without asking; the first after an edit equals the oracle), `augmentation_tests::a_file_an_augmentation_search_could_not_read_...` (the failed layer holds no augmenters).
103	
104	Mutation proof (`/tmp/claude-501/mutate-527b.sh`), each KILLED: `failed` demand not recorded; walk failure swallowed (`unwrap_or(None)`); scan failure swallowed (`.ok().flatten()`); failed parse kept in the layer as `None`; a read per caller; refusal not held; `transient` ignored; absence read as unavailable; `to_bytes` guard removed (kills the kept test). The `kept::save` check of its own survived (redundant with `to_bytes`) and was removed.
105	
106	Gates (exit codes):
107	
108	- `just lint doc-check machete typos`: 0.

## What

Two shared-state defects where a transient failure was stored as an answer. Both confirmed by tests that fail on `origin/main` (`f4a88f93`).

**1. A checker outage was kept as the component's answer** (`crates/core/src/pipeline/semantic_hook.rs`; audit shared-state hit 1, semantic-wire hit 1).

- Cause: `read_outcome` turned an outcome with no component and no fallback (`SemanticOutcome::unavailable`: timeout, crash, checker not running) into `Answered { component: None, diagnostics: [] }`, and `ask` inserted every `Answered` into `cache.answers`. The warning went to a once-per-session `warned` flag. Every later request until a source edit got structural props, no diagnostic, `awaits_checker` false.
- Fix: the notion is a type. `Settled` gains `Degraded(Vec<Diagnostic>)`; `read_outcome` returns it for an outcome that answers nothing. `ask` inserts only `Settled::Answered`. `refine` attaches a degraded request's diagnostics (each with `affects` = the component) to every answer it affects. The `warned` flag is gone. The next request asks the checker again.
- `awaits_checker` stays false on a degraded answer: a checker that stays down (`MAX_RESTARTS`, could not start) answers at once, so a host that re-asked on `awaits_checker` would loop. Not caching is what makes the next request ask again.

**2. A failed dependency read was persisted as "not exported"** (`crates/core/src/dependency_types.rs`; audit shared-state hit 4).

- Cause: `Loader::read` returned `None` on an I/O error, the `parsed` `OnceLock` stored `None`, `find_export_uncached` returned `None` without `cut`, the miss was cached, `learn`ed and written by `write_index` as `(module, name, None)`. Later runs trusted it while `package.json` was unchanged.
- Fix:
  - `read_text` returns `Err(Unreadable)` for a file that exists but cannot be read (still reports the Warning diagnostic once, as before). `parse_source` returns `Result<Option<_>, Unreadable>` and does not initialize the `parsed` cell on a failed read, so the next caller reads again.
  - `find_export_uncached` treats `Unreadable` as a cut (the cycle-cut mechanism): the miss is returned but neither kept, `learn`ed nor persisted.
  - The layer keeps only initialized `parsed` cells (`load`), so a session's next revision reads the file again instead of finding `None` in its parent.
  - `write_index` writes nothing when any dependency read failed in the run: an augmentation search's answer can hold the failure as an absence.

Invariant: a failure to read or to ask is unknown, never absence; nothing derived from it enters a cache, a layer or the index.

**2. A degraded answer is held as a short-lived refusal** (`crates/core/src/pipeline/semantic_hook.rs`). CONFIRMED.

- `AnswerCache::degraded`: `(key, stamp) -> (when, diagnostics)`, separate from `answers`. `find` returns `Found::Degraded` within `DEGRADED_RETRY` (30 s): the structural props plus the same diagnostics, without asking the checker. After it, or after `invalidate` (any source change, which clears it), the next request asks again; a recovered checker's answer is kept as usual.
- The clock is a `Clock` field (`Instant::now`), replaced in the unit test.
- `awaits_checker` stays false on a degraded answer: it means "ask again and you get the checker's props", which is false for 30 s; the Warning (`degradedBy` in the addon) tells the host the answer is degraded. A host that polled on `awaits_checker` would spin for the whole retry.

**3. Unavailability is a mark, not an absence** (`crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs`). CONFIRMED.

- `SemanticOutcome::unavailable: Option<Unavailable>`; `Unavailable(())` has a private field, so only `SemanticOutcome::unavailable(..)` can set it. `read_outcome` decides from it alone; an outcome with no entry for the key (a skipped target, a run past its heap budget) is `Settled::Answered` and kept.

**4. One read per file per load** (`parse_source`, `augmentation_scan`). CONFIRMED.

**5. A transient fallback is never kept** (`crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs`, `crates/semantic/src/lib.rs`, `crates/semantic/src/kept.rs`). CONFIRMED.

## Round 3

Review of `4d7187ab`: four findings, one root. Round 2 made a failed read abort the walk (`?`), so one unreadable file cost every answer the walk had already read or would read next; `origin/main` went on with the walk. Fixed at the class level: a walk or search over many files returns a **partial answer plus an incomplete mark**. It keeps everything read, goes on past the failed hop, gives this load the partial answer, and keeps it nowhere: not in the loader's maps, the layer or the index, the demand is not counted as followed, and a lazy session does not memoize a component that needed it.

The type: `Partial<T> { value, incomplete }` (`#[must_use]`) in `crates/core/src/dependency_types.rs`. `ReadFailed` stays the result of a read or parse of one file; every consumer over many files turns it into `incomplete`. The export walk's cycle cut and read failure share one `Unkept { cycle, unread }`: either one means the answer is returned but not kept; only `unread` makes the demand incomplete. `DependencyLayer::failed` holds the demands a read failure left unfollowed; `awaits_read(demands)` tells a caller that one of them may still load.

Findings (each test fails on `4d7187ab`, passes here):

1. **`chmod 000` does nothing as root** (low). CONFIRMED by inspection: root bypasses permission bits, so under a root runner or container the four read-failure tests read the file and fail their "the failed read is reported" assertion (or pass vacuously where none is made). Not reproduced (no root here). Fix: every read-failure test makes the file's bytes invalid UTF-8 (`make_unreadable`), which `std::fs::read_to_string` rejects for any user (`InvalidData`, not `NotFound`, so `ReadFailed`). The same fixture `an_unreadable_dependency_file_is_reported` already used. The tests are no longer `#[cfg(unix)]`, so they run on Windows too.
2. **The lazy memo kept a component resolved without a failed demand** (medium). On the base, `Card` asked again after the file read again was still `["title"]`, the memoized answer (first row; the `Tag`-first row reaches the same memo). Fix: `lazy_resolved` (`pipeline/revision/lazy.rs`) returns the answer without memoizing it while `layer.awaits_read(&missing)`; a demand whose load panicked still memoizes (it would never load). That exposed a second staleness: the layer chain kept reporting the old read failure after a later layer read the file, so the recovered answer differed from a fresh session's by one Warning. `panic_diagnostics` now drops a read failure for a file some layer of the chain has read since. - a warning list (`panics`): appended by every load that retried the file, copied whole by a flatten (A);
- uncovered demands (`failed`): only the demand that met the file, so a package file's failed import left its project demand followed (D);
- a `degraded` flag: the index gate;
- `parsed_data` membership: the rule that cleared a warning, which a scan-only read never satisfied (B).

On the checker side, `instantiate.rs` decided at its call sites that a rejected request was a verdict (C).

**The model: one `ReadLedger` per layer** (`crates/core/src/dependency_types/ledger.rs`), the only holder of the fact.

- Reads, by path: `Failed(warning)` or `Done`. Written only by `Loader::read`, the one function that reads a dependency file for a parse and a scan alike. `Done` is recorded only over an earlier failure. Within one load a failure stands, since the walk that met it is incomplete.
- Marks, by walk node (a demand, or a declaration `(file, name)` it claimed): `unread` (the demand's own walk passed an unreadable file) and `reaches` (the marked nodes below it). Each load records its edges (demand to claim, claim to claim, claim to spawned demand, a module demand to the demand that searched its scope), including edges to nodes a lower layer already followed. At the end it marks every node that reaches an unread walk, its own or one a lower layer marked that has not been followed since. A demand followed again that reaches none is marked clean, over its old mark. Edges are kept only for the load; a layer holds marks only when something failed.
- The newest entry in the chain wins. A flatten merges the chain's ledgers oldest first and drops what is clean.

Every decision is a query on it:

- Warnings: `read_warnings()`, one per path whose latest read failed, derived and never appended (A, B). `panics` holds panics only.
- Follow again: `missing()` gives the demands not followed and those whose own walk is unread (`awaits_retry`). `unread(roots)` gives the unread demands the roots lead to, through package files (D). `Loader::demand` follows a demand that awaits a retry once per load.
- Lazy memo: `lazy_resolved` adds `unread(roots)` to what it loads and memoizes nothing while it is non-empty. `grow` inherits no context memo while `any_unread()`: a memo built from a package declaration read without its nested file is read in a package file, which the old per-project-file `covers` check never looked at (found by the D test).
- Index: a cold load writes none when its ledger has a `Failed` read.

Deleted: `DependencyLayer::{failed, degraded}`, `Loader::{failed, read_failed}`, `awaits_read`, `inherited_failed`, the `parsed_data` filter in `panic_diagnostics`, and read warnings in `panics`.

Why marks are keyed by demand, not `path -> retry roots`: a later successful read of the path by another walk (a scan, another component) does not redo the walk that failed. Only following that demand again does. A path-keyed clear would memoize an answer whose walk is still incomplete.

**C: a rejection during instantiation is transient.** `instantiate::answer` sends every `CallError::Rejected` through `rejected_fallback_of`: a rejected layered snapshot, a rejection while answering on it, a rejection in `arguments_keep_their_meaning` or in reading the probe. The merge (`lib.rs` ~720-732) appends the fallbacks with their mark, so `SemanticOutcome::is_degraded` holds. `read_outcome` (`semantic_hook.rs`) returns `Settled::Degraded`, which is not cached, and `to_bytes` (`stored.rs`) refuses it. Those two files needed no change: they already decide from the mark alone.

- `lib.rs` `group_by_file`, not exported by its module: verdict (a fact of the source).
- `lib.rs` `answer_file`, `module_exports` is `Ok(None)` (not in the program): verdict.
- `lib.rs` `answer_file`, `module_exports` rejected: transient (unchanged).
- `lib.rs` `answer_file`, `Answer::Fallback` (the checker's answer cannot be read as props): verdict.
- `lib.rs` `answer_file`, `props_of` rejected: transient (unchanged).
- `instantiate.rs`, `layered` rejected: **transient** (was a verdict).
- `instantiate.rs`, `answer_layered` rejected: **transient** (was a verdict).
- `instantiate.rs`, the probe file not loaded by the checker: verdict (the snapshot's program).
- `instantiate.rs`, the instantiation has an error, is not declared, or its arguments mean something else in the probe file: verdict.
- `instantiate.rs`, `props_of_type` gives `Err(reason)`: verdict.
- `instantiate.rs`, `arguments_keep_their_meaning` or `read_probe` rejected: **transient** (was a verdict).

Findings. Each was confirmed by a test that fails on `dbff92cb` and passes here:

- **A (low): CONFIRMED.** `dependency_types::ledger::tests::a_file_that_stays_unreadable_is_reported_once_however_often_the_layer_grows`. `solo-kit/props.d.ts` stays unreadable through 11 growths, so the chain flattens at depth 8. After every growth `panic_diagnostics()` names exactly `[props.d.ts]`. Base: two copies after the first growth.
- **B (medium): CONFIRMED.** `a_stub_that_reads_again_through_a_scan_is_no_longer_reported`. `aug-kit/stub.d.ts` is a scan-only re-export stub. While it is unreadable the layer reports `[stub.d.ts]`. Once it reads, the next load reports `[]`, never parses the stub, and loads `inner.d.ts`'s augmentation past it. Base: `[stub.d.ts]`.
- **C (medium): CONFIRMED.** `instantiate::tests::a_rejected_instantiation_is_a_transient_fallback`, on a real checker. The snapshot is released first, so `layered` is rejected ("snapshot 1 not found"). Fallbacks are `[("Poly", true)]` and `is_degraded()` holds. Base: `[("Poly", false)]`.

Once it reads, `Card` equals a fresh session's (props and diagnostics): `["own", "title", "tone"]`, no warning. Base: `["own", "title"]`, memoized.

**Scope**: edit only the files the brief names; if another must change, stop and say which and why. Never ask the user questions; if blocked, report what blocks and what you tried. Do not wait on background work.

- Guards are ALLOW-lists: handle a closed set of proven forms; everything else is Unknown/Declined (never "complete", "none", "exact"). No `_ =>` arms in decisions over node/type kinds.
- Write the slice's invariants in the PR body (unknown unless proven; by binding not spelling; every read recorded; one owner; wired or not defined).
- Grammar sweep: list every syntax/type form the code can receive and show each is handled or declined (exhaustive match, or a generated test over the grammar with the checker/TS API as oracle). Generate over the grammar, not over past findings.
- Mutation proof: remove each guard/dependency; a test must fail. Report which you tried (cargo mutants --in-diff works).
- Before reporting: run `/code-review medium` on the explicit SHA range, then try to break your own change with inputs the diff did not mention (computed keys, symbols, getters, overloads, re-exports, shadowing, optional chains, declare/abstract, conditional types, lone surrogates).

Wall time matters most to the user; memory (peak RSS) is also important; CPU seconds are a tie-breaker, not a goal. Stated 2026-11-23 while deciding whether rayon threads should be capped or dynamic.

**Why:** the user feels wall time, and Storybook runs beside Vite, the IDE and the TypeScript server, so memory and wasted CPU matter on their machine and on few-core CI runners. A change that lowers CPU but raises wall time is a loss (a fixed rayon cap of 4 cut CPU 17-36% on four corpora but doubled Chakra's wall time).

**How to apply:** accept no wall regression on any corpus; then take the lower peak RSS; then lower CPU. Judge by the addon's first-answer latency (150 ms budget) and per-story median (`gate_harness first-answer`), not only the whole-project `extract` wall time the weekly records. Measure on a quiet machine (load under ~10, swap not full) or compare CPU and counts; see [[measure-memory-and-time]] and [[measurement-must-match-real-consumer]].

Three read-only audits on 2026-11-24 (reports committed on branch `docs/review-checklist` under `docs/audits/2026-11-24-*.md`) found that our recurring review findings are one root problem in three places: a DECISION is made from something that is not evidence. Extractor: a spelling (PascalCase callee, name lists, `contains("Component")`) or a raw expression. Wire boundary (crates/semantic): an ABSENT or defaulted field read as a value (`#[serde(default)]`, `unwrap_or(false)`, tsrs omits empty fields). Caches and sessions: a DEGRADED result (timeout, read failure, heap budget, nesting cut) stored as authoritative. The rules already exist in prose (CONTRIBUTING 'Before you push', ADR 0025-0028: by binding not spelling, one owner per decision, unknown unless proven, always emit a Diagnostic when degrading); nothing enforces them in code.

**Why:** reviews found 3 + 3 + 5 findings per PR in the same classes; each fix moved the problem (validating on a shared cache primed it the other way). Fixing per site does not converge.

**How to apply (direction, in this order):** (1) failing-first counter-example suites (extractor M10: every snippet in the audit becomes a row asserting exact output); (2) make invalid states unrepresentable: `ComponentEvidence` required to build a `ComponentMapping`, a typed `Peeled` (Transparent | Instantiated | Asserted) with one exhaustive match, `Known<T>` for decoded wire fields, a `Degraded` marker on outcomes that no cache or kept answer stores, `CallError::Contract` for undecodable responses with its own code; (3) one owner modules (`extractor/decide.rs`, `semantic/src/wire.rs` with one tsrs version-pin test, one `Memo` abstraction); (4) architecture tests (grep-based Rust tests, no new scripts) that fail on a catch-all arm or a name literal in a decision, `unwrap_or(false)` on wire values, text matching of messages, statics in non-test code; (5) determinism as a tested property: differential tests with separate state per consumer as oracle, session equals cold extract under random edit scripts. Amend ADR 0027/0026: 'a name is a candidate filter, never a verdict'. Related: [[diagnose-after-three-findings]], [[workers-run-full-lint-gate]].

description: "After three findings on one PR stop routing spot fixes: tabulate them, name root causes (one decision with two owners, state keyed wrong, singletons), decide if the design must change"
metadata:

  type: feedback
  originSessionId: ad4b3461-bb6f-49f0-bb4d-997d9b8887ba

---

On 2026-11-14 the user said they were "disappointed that you're not taking a step back to understand the patterns, consider the architecture and our models" after the Storybook live-upgrade PR (#462) collected 11 findings over 5 rounds that I routed one at a time as spot fixes. I had promised a model-based approach "if another finding appears" and still patched the next one.

**Why:** findings arrive serially from a reviewer that sees a slice each round; workers capped at 25-35 calls patch the symptom. The 11 findings shared four root causes: no explicit lifecycle model (state scattered across flags keyed by the wrong dimension: component instead of component+revision+key+client), decisions made in two places (lazy vs eager, structural vs checker diagnostics, two dev servers), last-writer-wins singletons where truth is a per-client set, and TypeScript re-deriving what the Rust core already owns. Same smell as #455 (two walkers decide eligibility), #459 (two paths feed the kept answer), #458.

**How to apply:**
- Third finding on a PR: stop; make a table of the findings, name the root causes, ask 'is one decision made or held in two places?' and 'what is the state machine and who owns it?'.
- Remedy shape: one owner for each decision (prefer the Rust core's merged answer over re-deriving in TS), one explicit reducer (pure state x event -> state x effects), and a model-based/property test of the invariants after quiescence, with the earlier findings as named regression sequences.
- Give such a worker room (cap ~100 calls, Opus); caps suit mechanical work, not stateful mechanisms.
- Before accepting any worker fix ask: is the same fact decided or held anywhere else?

**Second instance, 2026-11-15 (#467, tsrs_module swapped for oxc_resolver):** five findings in five rounds, each in glue code that re-created an old behaviour (symlink canonicalization, `.cts` conditions, relative tsconfig, fingerprint inputs, a `baseUrl` fallback that guessed which rule answered from whether the path contained `node_modules`). I called the root cause settled twice and was wrong twice. The user: "How are you not guarding against these coming up???"

**Why:** a behaviour-preserving library swap was gated by a single-run identity diff on two fixtures, which cannot see cross-run cache staleness or inputs the fixtures lack; fix rounds added new heuristic code that nothing exercised; the Entire reviewer was the first real review. The swap's premise ("same results, less code") was false: tsrs follows TypeScript 7 (no `baseUrl` for bare specifiers) where the old resolver followed TypeScript 6, and the PR grew to +768/-222.

**How to apply:**
- Before a swap: inventory every behaviour of the replaced component that the code relies on (options, conditions, symlinks, config inheritance, cache keys) and diff old against new over the cross-product, not two fixtures.
- Before pushing any worker branch: read the diff myself for heuristics (a rule inferred from path shape, a guess) and run `/code-review` on it; do not let the Entire reviewer be the first review.
- At the third finding re-test the premise (does the swap still delete more than it adds?), not only the root cause; if not, close the PR.

**Third instance, 2026-11-15 (about 50 findings across trails 404/405):** the user said "consider all of the findings together, architecturally and semantically ... make sure the agents won't find even more things". Eight root classes (silence read as evidence, lossy model asserting exactness, spelling instead of binding, derived state outside the dependency model, one decision with two owners, host assumptions, hand-tuned policy with no reference model, contract drift / fields never populated). Table: ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/shrink/findings-synthesis.md.

**Why:** guards were DENY-lists (enumerate the wrong cases found so far), so each new grammar form (a `[Symbol.iterator]` key) produced the next finding; about 40% of the raw count was the same code repeated in stacked child PRs.

**How to apply:**
- Design guards as ALLOW-lists: a closed set of proven forms, everything else Unknown/Declined; exhaustive matches, no wildcard arms in decisions.
- Run the pre-push gate in worker-contract.md (invariants, grammar sweep with the checker/TS API as oracle, mutation proof, adversarial pass, then /code-review) before any push; generate tests over the grammar, not over past findings.
- Merge stacks in order and retarget children; do not keep a stack alive across review rounds.

See [[resolve-findings-when-fixed]] and [[worker-token-budget]].

**Artifacts**: PR body with `## What`, `## Evidence` (numbers, exit codes, what was diffed), `## Not verified`, last line the session url; the lead publishes it unedited. Final message <= 120 words: branch, head SHA (ls-remote verified), body path, blockers.

**Pre-push gate (the reviewer must find nothing new)**:
- Guards are ALLOW-lists: handle a closed set of proven forms; everything else is Unknown/Declined (never "complete", "none", "exact"). No `_ =>` arms in decisions over node/type kinds.
- Write the slice's invariants in the PR body (unknown unless proven; by binding not spelling; every read recorded; one owner; wired or not defined).
- Grammar sweep: list every syntax/type form the code can receive and show each is handled or declined (exhaustive match, or a generated test over the grammar with the checker/TS API as oracle). Generate over the grammar, not over past findings.
- Mutation proof: remove each guard/dependency; a test must fail. Report which you tried (cargo mutants --in-diff works).
- Before reporting: run `/code-review medium` on the explicit SHA range, then try to break your own change with inputs the diff did not mention (computed keys, symbols, getters, overloads, re-exports, shadowing, optional chains, declare/abstract, conditional types, lone surrogates).

---

Wall time matters most to the user; memory (peak RSS) is also important; CPU seconds are a tie-breaker, not a goal. Stated 2026-11-23 while deciding whether rayon threads should be capped or dynamic.

**Why:** the user feels wall time, and Storybook runs beside Vite, the IDE and the TypeScript server, so memory and wasted CPU matter on their machine and on few-core CI runners. A change that lowers CPU but raises wall time is a loss (a fixed rayon cap of 4 cut CPU 17-36% on four corpora but doubled Chakra's wall time).

**How to apply:** accept no wall regression on any corpus; then take the lower peak RSS; then lower CPU. Judge by the addon's first-answer latency (150 ms budget) and per-story median (`gate_harness first-answer`), not only the whole-project `extract` wall time the weekly records. Measure on a quiet machine (load under ~10, swap not full) or compare CPU and counts; see [[measure-memory-and-time]] and [[measurement-must-match-real-consumer]].

metadata:

---

Three read-only audits on 2026-11-24 (reports committed on branch `docs/review-checklist` under `docs/audits/2026-11-24-*.md`) found that our recurring review findings are one root problem in three places: a DECISION is made from something that is not evidence. Extractor: a spelling (PascalCase callee, name lists, `contains("Component")`) or a raw expression. Wire boundary (crates/semantic): an ABSENT or defaulted field read as a value (`#[serde(default)]`, `unwrap_or(false)`, tsrs omits empty fields). Caches and sessions: a DEGRADED result (timeout, read failure, heap budget, nesting cut) stored as authoritative. The rules already exist in prose (CONTRIBUTING 'Before you push', ADR 0025-0028: by binding not spelling, one owner per decision, unknown unless proven, always emit a Diagnostic when degrading); nothing enforces them in code.

**Why:** reviews found 3 + 3 + 5 findings per PR in the same classes; each fix moved the problem (validating on a shared cache primed it the other way). Fixing per site does not converge.

**How to apply (direction, in this order):** (1) failing-first counter-example suites (extractor M10: every snippet in the audit becomes a row asserting exact output); (2) make invalid states unrepresentable: `ComponentEvidence` required to build a `ComponentMapping`, a typed `Peeled` (Transparent | Instantiated | Asserted) with one exhaustive match, `Known<T>` for decoded wire fields, a `Degraded` marker on outcomes that no cache or kept answer stores, `CallError::Contract` for undecodable responses with its own code; (3) one owner modules (`extractor/decide.rs`, `semantic/src/wire.rs` with one tsrs version-pin test, one `Memo` abstraction); (4) architecture tests (grep-based Rust tests, no new scripts) that fail on a catch-all arm or a name literal in a decision, `unwrap_or(false)` on wire values, text matching of messages, statics in non-test code; (5) determinism as a tested property: differential tests with separate state per consumer as oracle, session equals cold extract under random edit scripts. Amend ADR 0027/0026: 'a name is a candidate filter, never a verdict'. Related: [[diagnose-after-three-findings]], [[workers-run-full-lint-gate]].

name: diagnose-after-three-findings
description: "After three findings on one PR stop routing spot fixes: tabulate them, name root causes (one decision with two owners, state keyed wrong, singletons), decide if the design must change"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: ad4b3461-bb6f-49f0-bb4d-997d9b8887ba
  modified: 2026-11-16T01:05:54.318Z
---

On 2026-11-14 the user said they were "disappointed that you're not taking a step back to understand the patterns, consider the architecture and our models" after the Storybook live-upgrade PR (#462) collected 11 findings over 5 rounds that I routed one at a time as spot fixes. I had promised a model-based approach "if another finding appears" and still patched the next one.

**Why:** findings arrive serially from a reviewer that sees a slice each round; workers capped at 25-35 calls patch the symptom. The 11 findings shared four root causes: no explicit lifecycle model (state scattered across flags keyed by the wrong dimension: component instead of component+revision+key+client), decisions made in two places (lazy vs eager, structural vs checker diagnostics, two dev servers), last-writer-wins singletons where truth is a per-client set, and TypeScript re-deriving what the Rust core already owns. Same smell as #455 (two walkers decide eligibility), #459 (two paths feed the kept answer), #458.

**How to apply:**
- Third finding on a PR: stop; make a table of the findings, name the root causes, ask 'is one decision made or held in two places?' and 'what is the state machine and who owns it?'.
- Remedy shape: one owner for each decision (prefer the Rust core's merged answer over re-deriving in TS), one explicit reducer (pure state x event -> state x effects), and a model-based/property test of the invariants after quiescence, with the earlier findings as named regression sequences.
- Give such a worker room (cap ~100 calls, Opus); caps suit mechanical work, not stateful mechanisms.
- Before accepting any worker fix ask: is the same fact decided or held anywhere else?

**Second instance, 2026-11-15 (#467, tsrs_module swapped for oxc_resolver):** five findings in five rounds, each in glue code that re-created an old behaviour (symlink canonicalization, `.cts` conditions, relative tsconfig, fingerprint inputs, a `baseUrl` fallback that guessed which rule answered from whether the path contained `node_modules`). I called the root cause settled twice and was wrong twice. The user: "How are you not guarding against these coming up???"

**Why:** a behaviour-preserving library swap was gated by a single-run identity diff on two fixtures, which cannot see cross-run cache staleness or inputs the fixtures lack; fix rounds added new heuristic code that nothing exercised; the Entire reviewer was the first real review. The swap's premise ("same results, less code") was false: tsrs follows TypeScript 7 (no `baseUrl` for bare specifiers) where the old resolver followed TypeScript 6, and the PR grew to +768/-222.

**How to apply:**
- Before a swap: inventory every behaviour of the replaced component that the code relies on (options, conditions, symlinks, config inheritance, cache keys) and diff old against new over the cross-product, not two fixtures.
- Before pushing any worker branch: read the diff myself for heuristics (a rule inferred from path shape, a guess) and run `/code-review` on it; do not let the Entire reviewer be the first review.
- At the third finding re-test the premise (does the swap still delete more than it adds?), not only the root cause; if not, close the PR.

**Third instance, 2026-11-15 (about 50 findings across trails 404/405):** the user said "consider all of the findings together, architecturally and semantically ... make sure the agents won't find even more things". Eight root classes (silence read as evidence, lossy model asserting exactness, spelling instead of binding, derived state outside the dependency model, one decision with two owners, host assumptions, hand-tuned policy with no reference model, contract drift / fields never populated). Table: ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/shrink/findings-synthesis.md.

**Why:** guards were DENY-lists (enumerate the wrong cases found so far), so each new grammar form (a `[Symbol.iterator]` key) produced the next finding; about 40% of the raw count was the same code repeated in stacked child PRs.

**How to apply:**
- Design guards as ALLOW-lists: a closed set of proven forms, everything else Unknown/Declined; exhaustive matches, no wildcard arms in decisions.
- Run the pre-push gate in worker-contract.md (invariants, grammar sweep with the checker/TS API as oracle, mutation proof, adversarial pass, then /code-review) before any push; generate tests over the grammar, not over past findings.
- Merge stacks in order and retarget children; do not keep a stack alive across review rounds.

See [[resolve-findings-when-fixed]] and [[worker-token-budget]].

4	cargo/caliper-docgen-napi: patch
5	npm/caliper-docgen: patch
6	---
7	
8	**A checker outage or an unreadable dependency file no longer sticks to a component.** The next request or run asks again and gets the real answer.
9	
10	- Why it matters: in a watch or Storybook session, one checker timeout, crash or rejected request used to leave the component on its structural props until a source file changed, and a rejected request was also kept on disk as the checker's answer. A dependency `.d.ts` that could not be read once (too many open files, an install racing the run) used to be kept as "not exported", in the session until it restarted and in the dependency index for later runs.
11	- What you see now: every answer the failed checker affects carries its warning. The component is asked again 30 seconds later or after the next source-file change; until then a request gets the structural props and the warning at once, without waiting on a checker that just failed. A run that cannot read a dependency file still warns, and keeps everything it could read: a type a later `export *` target declares, and the React augmentations of the other files. The session's next request and the next run read the file again, and once it reads, the component has its full props and the warning is gone.
12	- Also covered: a prop that a package's type inherits from another file of the package that could not be read, and a generic component (`as` props) whose instantiation the checker rejected. Each is asked again on the next request instead of being kept without the prop.
13	- A file that stays unreadable is reported once in each answer, however many requests a session makes.
14	
15	**Breaking:** for Rust users of `caliper-docgen-core`, `SemanticOutcome` has a new field `unavailable` (set only by `SemanticOutcome::unavailable`) and `SemanticFallback` a new field `transient`. A struct literal that names every field no longer compiles: add `unavailable: None` and `transient: false`, or build the outcome with `..Default::default()`.

A dependency `.d.ts` that could not be read once (too many open files, an install racing the run) used to be kept as "not exported", in the session until it restarted and in the dependency index for later runs.
- What you see now: every answer the failed checker affects carries its warning. The component is asked again 30 seconds later or after the next source-file change; until then a request gets the structural props and the warning at once, without waiting on a checker that just failed. A run that cannot read a dependency file still warns, and keeps everything it could read: a type a later `export *` target declares, and the React augmentations of the other files. The session's next request and the next run read the file again, and once it reads, the component has its full props and the warning is gone.
- Also covered: a prop that a package's type inherits from another file of the package that could not be read, and a generic component (`as` props) whose instantiation the checker rejected. Each is asked again on the next request instead of being kept without the prop.
- A file that stays unreadable is reported once in each answer, however many requests a session makes.

**Breaking:** for Rust users of `caliper-docgen-core`, `SemanticOutcome` has a new field `unavailable` (set only by `SemanticOutcome::unavailable`) and `SemanticFallback` a new field `transient`. A struct literal that names every field no longer compiles: add `unavailable: None` and `transient: false`, or build the outcome with `..Default::default()`.
